version.changelog:
- Chart generation now outputs PNG images instead of SVG, and responses will prioritize sending images as attachments.
- Chart script API updated: use `png_markdown`, `png_data_uri`, or `png_path` for image output.
- Data model version downgraded from 2.1 to 2.0, removing USD conversion fields.
- Report aggregation and chart currency display are now consistently based on `default_currency`, with missing exchange rates triggering warnings.
- Documentation streamlined with a focus on key commands and clearer usage instructions.

llm.summary: The skill's files, instructions, and requested resources are coherent with an expense-tracking/bookkeeping purpose — it reads/writes a local ledger under ~/.qclaw/workspace/expense-ledger and generates reports and exports, with no external credentials or network calls requested.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it advertises: it parses messages and stores an expense ledger locally at ~/.qclaw/workspace/expense-ledger, generates charts and CSV/JSON exports, and requires no credentials. Before installing/using: (1) be aware all ledger data and exports will be written to your home directory under ~/.qclaw — back them up or remove them if needed; (2) inspect the rest of ledger.py/charts.py for any subprocess calls (charts.py imports subprocess) to ensure no commands are constructed from untrusted input; (3) if you plan to open exported HTML or CSV files in a browser or Excel, treat raw fields (user-provided notes/raw input) as untrusted content; (4) there are no network calls or secret-exfiltration indicators in the visible files, but if you need higher assurance, run the scripts in a restricted environment (container or VM) or review the truncated portions of ledger.py/charts.py before use.
